topic: Rajasthan HC: a contractual woman employee cannot be denied maternity leave just because she is on contract - Section 27, Maternity Benefit Act overrides contract terms; 180 days granted (Smt. Shivangi Khandelwal v. State of Rajasthan, S.B. CWP No. 1561/2023, 2026:RJ-JD:49861, 2026 LiveLaw (Raj) 449)

slides.title: On contract? You still get **maternity leave**
slides.subtitle: Being a contractual employee is **not** a valid reason, by itself, to refuse maternity benefits.
slides.cite: **Shivangi Khandelwal v. State of Rajasthan**, 2026:RJ-JD:49861 · Justice Bipin Gupta

slides.label: The case
slides.title: Leave refused over **one contract clause**
bullets: She was hired as a **consultant** by the Rajasthan State Pollution Control Board on a one-year contract from August 2022.
She asked for **six months** of maternity leave from 26 December 2022, on her doctor's advice.
It was refused because her appointment order allowed **only government holidays**, and no other leave.

slides.label: What the court said
slides.title: Maternity benefit is a **legal right**
bullets: Whether a woman is regular, casual or contractual is **not, by itself**, a ground to deny maternity benefits if the legal conditions are met.
A contract term that clashes with the Maternity Benefit Act **cannot override** the Act.
The refusal relied only on the contract clause and never checked whether she was **actually eligible**.
slides.note: **Law fact:** Section 27 of the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 gives the Act **overriding effect** over any contrary agreement or contract of service.

slides.label: The result
slides.title: **180 days** of maternity benefits
bullets: The High Court **quashed** the rejection letter and allowed her petition.
The employer must give her **180 days** of maternity benefits from 26 December 2022, with the remuneration due under the law.
This must be done within **three months** of receiving a certified copy of the judgment.
slides.note: **Law fact:** In 2000, the Supreme Court held that women on **muster roll or casual** work are also entitled to maternity benefits (MCD v. Female Workers).

slides.label: Keep in mind
slides.title: The **legal conditions** still apply
bullets: The ruling does not mean every claim is automatic. The woman must still meet the **conditions under the law**.
Here, the whole leave period she asked for fell **within her contract term**.
This post is for information only, not legal advice.

caption:
Working on contract does not take away your right to maternity leave 🤰⚖️

The Rajasthan High Court has said that the type of job a woman holds, whether regular, casual or contractual, cannot by itself be a reason to deny her maternity benefits when the legal conditions are met. A clause in a contract cannot override the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, because Section 27 of the Act gives it overriding effect over any contrary agreement.

In this case, a woman was hired as a consultant by the Rajasthan State Pollution Control Board on a one-year contract in August 2022. She asked for six months of maternity leave from 26 December 2022. It was refused only because her appointment order allowed government holidays and no other leave. The court said the refusal never examined whether she was actually eligible, and her whole leave period fell within her contract term.

The High Court quashed the rejection and directed that she be given 180 days of maternity benefits, with the remuneration due under the law, within three months of the employer receiving a certified copy of the judgment. Each case still depends on its own facts and the conditions under the law.

Case: Smt. Shivangi Khandelwal v. State of Rajasthan & Anr., S.B. Civil Writ Petition No. 1561/2023 | 2026:RJ-JD:49861 | 2026 LiveLaw (Raj) 449 | Justice Bipin Gupta, Rajasthan High Court (Jodhpur)
